sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook, Chapter 2: Measurement Process Characterization
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1.2, 2.4.3.2, 2.4.4.1–2.4.4.3, and 2.4.5.3. The full Chapter 2 PDF was fetched and verified; the relevant check-standard, nested-design, variation, and drift sections were read, including the assigned gauge-study ranges PDF pp. 208–238 and 243–283.

contents.name: Check standards and repeated readings across days
contents.support: The Handbook describes check-standard measurements as a way to observe the process over time and distinguishes short-term repeat readings from measurements across days. The item adopts an explicit finite nested model and defines its index roles locally.

contents.name: Repeatability, day-to-day reproducibility, and run-to-run stability
contents.support: The Handbook organizes measurement variation by short-term repetitions, days, and longer runs. The item states the scope of each term and warns that the terminology is not universal.

contents.name: Detecting calibration drift with check standards
contents.support: The Handbook states that linear-calibration drift can be monitored with three or more check standards. The example uses three stable standards and verifies only the stipulated arithmetic.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 5 Notes: Estimation of Group Effects
sources.locator: Full 11-page note fetched and verified; read §3.1, PDF p. 4, for group sample-mean variance and §4.1, PDF p. 8, for the random-groups model and target-population interpretation.

contents.name: Group-mean variance and random versus fixed group interpretation
contents.support: The note states the within-group sample-mean variance and distinguishes a superpopulation of sampled groups from a finite set treated as fixed. The local theorem proves the unbalanced nested variance formula from moment assumptions only.

contents.name: Scalar random-groups model and common within-group covariance
contents.support: The note gives the scalar shared-random-intercept structure. The local proof supplies the finite-moment result without importing the note's Gaussian distribution assumption.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 6 Notes: Linear Mixed-Effects Models
sources.locator: Full 16-page note fetched and verified; read §2, PDF pp. 4–5, for fixed/random effect roles and §§4.1–4.3, PDF pp. 8–10, for within-group covariance and its random-intercept specialization.

contents.name: Fixed and random effects in the general mixed model
contents.support: The note distinguishes fixed coefficients from group-level random departures. The item makes random-versus-fixed batch status depend explicitly on the target and sampling design.

contents.name: Within-group covariance from a shared random effect
contents.support: The note expands the marginal covariance for random intercepts and slopes. The local theorem proves its scalar random-intercept case directly for independent finite-second-moment terms, without Gaussianity.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook, Chapter 2: Measurement Process Characterization
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1.2 and 2.4.5.3; the full 426-page Chapter 2 PDF was fetched and verified, and these check-standard and linear-calibration-drift sections were read. Section 2.4.5.3 is in PDF pp. 243–283.

contents.name: Three or more check standards for monitoring linear-calibration drift
contents.support: The example explicitly stipulates three stable standards and calculates day-specific slopes and pooled-line residuals; no NIST estimator or test is imported.

contents.name: Check-standard stability and process monitoring
contents.support: The source motivates repeatedly measuring fixed reference artifacts as process checks. The example states stability and all responses as assumptions rather than empirical findings.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of Measurement Data — Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement
sources.locator: Full 134-page Guide fetched and verified; read Annex H.3.1–H.3.3, PDF pp. 100–102 / printed pp. 89–91, for reference-standard linear calibration, least-squares fitting, and residuals.

contents.name: H.3 Linear calibration of a thermometer using reference temperatures
contents.support: The Guide formulates a line from reference measurements by least squares and identifies residuals as checks on the linear model. The local example performs its own complete finite minimization and makes no uncertainty claim.

sources.title: Fan Li, STA610 Lecture 6 Notes: Linear Mixed-Effects Models
sources.locator: Full 16-page note fetched and verified; read §§1.1–1.2, PDF pp. 2–3, for heterogeneous group slopes and the common-line pooling caution, and §2, PDF pp. 4–5, for fixed/random effect roles.

contents.name: Group-specific slopes and the common-line pooling warning
contents.support: The lecture shows that group slopes may differ and that pooling all groups into one line ignores such differences. The local example verifies a stipulated two-day calibration calculation without importing its fitted-model assumptions.
